schema.description: {{COMPANY_NAME}} reusable Merlino Catalogue threat-profile template for System Integrator / MSP organisations. data.Name: TP-09 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Acquire leaked, stolen or infostealer-derived credentials for SaaS users, administrators and customer-facing personnel. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: SaaS data-theft operations are identity-centric. Stolen credentials can provide immediate access to CRM, M365, ticketing, source repositories and cloud storage. Applicability: Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: SSO credentials, SaaS administrators, Customer-facing users. Detection opportunities: Leaked credential monitoring; Risk detections. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Credential exposure response.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: SaaS data-theft operations are identity-centric. Stolen credentials can provide immediate access to CRM, M365, ticketing, source repositories and cloud storage. Threat-led context: M-Trends 2026 highlights identity, OAuth token and SaaS compromise as major data-theft paths. Applicability=Core; Phase=Targeting; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-09 | Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Roles
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Identify users likely to administer CRM, M365, support systems, cloud storage and data platforms. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: High-privilege SaaS administrators can authorize connected applications, exports and API access. Applicability: Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: SaaS admins, CRM admins, M365 admins, Data owners. Detection opportunities: Targeting intelligence. Defensive considerations: Dedicated privileged identities; PIM where available.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: High-privilege SaaS administrators can authorize connected applications, exports and API access. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Core; Phase=Targeting; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Safe Links.

data.Name: TP-09 | Social Engineering: Impersonation
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Impersonate internal IT, help desk, SaaS support or another trusted party. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: SaaS compromise often relies on the victim believing a legitimate administrator is guiding them through a normal configuration step. Applicability: Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Social Engineering. Primary assets at risk: Employees, Help desk, SaaS admins. Detection opportunities: User-reported impersonation. Defensive considerations: Out-of-band verification.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Threat-led context: Salesforce Data Exfiltration actors impersonated IT support. Applicability=Core; Phase=Social Engineering; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. data.Name: TP-09 | Steal Application Access Token
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Steal OAuth tokens, personal access tokens or connected-application tokens. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: OAuth and API tokens can provide long-lived programmatic access and can survive password changes. Applicability: Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Token Theft. Primary assets at risk: OAuth tokens, PATs, Connected app tokens, API tokens. Detection opportunities: Token use from unusual client/IP. Defensive considerations: Short-lived tokens; Token scoping; Rotation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: OAuth and API tokens can provide long-lived programmatic access and can survive password changes. Threat-led context: M-Trends 2026 highlights long-lived OAuth tokens; UNC6395 used compromised Salesloft Drift OAuth tokens to reach Salesforce. Applicability=Core; Phase=Token Theft; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

Defensive considerations: Managed devices; Session protection.

data.Name: TP-09 | Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Add attacker-controlled secrets or certificates to cloud applications or service principals. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Additional credentials can preserve API access after user credential remediation. Applicability: Cloud / SaaS. SaaS data-theft phase: Persistence. Primary assets at risk: App registrations, Service principals, Automation identities. Detection opportunities: New secret/certificate. Defensive considerations: Workload federation; Credential-change alerts.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Additional credentials can preserve API access after user credential remediation. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Cloud / SaaS; Phase=Persistence; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Privileged Identity; Phase=Persistence; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-09 | Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Create forwarding rules to send ongoing mailbox content externally. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Forwarding creates continuous SaaS data leakage with minimal interactive activity. Applicability: M365. SaaS data-theft phase: Persistent Collection. Primary assets at risk: Exchange Online. Detection opportunities: External forwarding rule. Defensive considerations: Block unnecessary forwarding; Rule alerts.

Primary assets at risk: CRM admin, M365 admin, Support platform admin. Detection opportunities: Portal access from rare device/location. Defensive considerations: Managed admin devices; PIM.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Interactive access through normal dashboards can blend with legitimate administration. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Core; Phase=SaaS Discovery; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: List files, blobs and objects accessible to the compromised account or application. data.Description: Use Python scripts or custom applications to query SaaS APIs and extract data. data.Name: TP-09 | Data from Information Repositories: Messaging Applications
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Mine Teams, Slack and other messaging systems for sensitive data, credentials, customer discussions and incident-response information. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Chat systems expose both valuable data and context that can help attackers evade defenders or identify new targets. Applicability: Collaboration Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: Teams, Slack, Messaging. Detection opportunities: Bulk chat export; Graph/eDiscovery message access. Defensive considerations: Out-of-band IR channel; Least privilege.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Chat systems expose both valuable data and context that can help attackers evade defenders or identify new targets. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Collaboration Core; Phase=Collection; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-09 | Data from Information Repositories: Databases
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Query or export data from SaaS and cloud databases such as Snowflake, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB or other repositories. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Database theft can expose large volumes of PII, financial, credential and customer data and is directly associated with extortion campaigns. Applicability: Database Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: Snowflake, Azure SQL, Cloud databases, Application databases. Detection opportunities: Bulk query/export; Rare identity exporting large datasets. Defensive considerations: DB least privilege; MFA where supported; Query/export monitoring.

Detection opportunities: Mass download; Unusual API client. Defensive considerations: DLP; Storage least privilege; Versioning.

data.Name: TP-09 | Automated Collection
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Automate retrieval of CRM, email, cloud files, database records and support data. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Modern SaaS extortion relies on fast API-driven collection to maximize theft before tokens are revoked. Applicability: Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: CRM, M365, Databases, Cloud storage. Detection opportunities: High-rate API queries; Sequential bulk export. Defensive considerations: API behavior analytics; Rate controls.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Modern SaaS extortion relies on fast API-driven collection to maximize theft before tokens are revoked. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Core; Phase=Collection; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-09 | Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Code Repository
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Upload stolen data to an attacker-controlled code repository. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Repository APIs are commonly trusted and may provide cover from developer environments. Applicability: Developer / SaaS. SaaS data-theft phase: Exfiltration. Primary assets at risk: GitHub/GitLab, Stolen data. Detection opportunities: New repo/upload by unusual identity. Defensive considerations: DLP; Restrict repo creation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Repository APIs are commonly trusted and may provide cover from developer environments. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Developer / SaaS; Phase=Exfiltration; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-09 | Transfer Data to Cloud Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Use native cloud sharing, ownership transfer, sync, snapshot copy or anonymous links to move data to an attacker-controlled account in the same or another cloud service context. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This can bypass network-centric exfiltration monitoring because the transfer occurs inside legitimate cloud-provider APIs. Applicability: Cloud Native. SaaS data-theft phase: Exfiltration. Primary assets at risk: OneDrive, SharePoint, Cloud storage, Snapshots. Detection opportunities: External sharing; SAS/anonymous link creation; Cross-account transfer. Defensive considerations: External sharing restrictions; DLP; Sharing alerts.

data.Name: TP-09 | Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Use HTTPS for SaaS API access, data transfer and attacker-controlled collection infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: SaaS data theft is naturally web-protocol heavy and can blend with normal cloud traffic. Applicability: Core. SaaS data-theft phase: Exfiltration. Primary assets at risk: HTTPS, SaaS APIs. Detection opportunities: Unusual scripted user agents; Large POST/download patterns. Defensive considerations: Proxy analytics; API monitoring.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: SaaS data theft is naturally web-protocol heavy and can blend with normal cloud traffic. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Core; Phase=Exfiltration; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: A privileged SaaS attacker can reduce visibility before bulk collection or extortion. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to SaaS-centric data theft and extortion. Applicability=Privileged SaaS; Phase=Defense Impairment; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-09 models cloud/SaaS data theft where the principal objective is access to, collection of and exfiltration of data rather than endpoint encryption. It covers SSO/session/OAuth compromise, malicious connected applications, CRM, Microsoft 365, messaging, code repositories, databases, cloud storage, support/ticketing data, programmatic API collection, native cloud sharing and data-theft extortion. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-09 | Account Access Removal
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Disable legitimate administrators or users to delay response after data theft. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Lockout can preserve attacker access and slow token/application revocation. Applicability: Privileged SaaS. SaaS data-theft phase: Impact. Primary assets at risk: SaaS admins, Data owners. Detection opportunities: Admin disable/delete. Defensive considerations: Break-glass accounts; Out-of-band recovery.

data.Name: TP-09 | Data Destruction
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Delete cloud or SaaS data after exfiltration to increase pressure or sabotage recovery. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Data-theft extortion can include destructive follow-on actions even when ransomware encryption is absent. Applicability: Destructive Extortion Conditional. SaaS data-theft phase: Impact. Primary assets at risk: Cloud files, CRM data, Databases. Detection opportunities: Mass deletion; Bulk record destruction. Defensive considerations: Retention/versioning; Immutable backups.

data.Name: TP-09 | Trusted Relationship
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-09 SaaS / Data Exfiltration / Data-Theft Extortion
data.Description: Leverage compromised SaaS vendors, applications or integrations to access downstream customer data. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: M-Trends 2026 highlights compromise of third-party SaaS vendors and use of stolen keys/PATs to pivot into downstream customers. Applicability: Third-Party SaaS. SaaS data-theft phase: Initial Access / Pivot. Primary assets at risk: SaaS integrations, Vendor apps, Customer tenants. Detection opportunities: Vendor-token anomalies; Unexpected app access. Defensive considerations: Third-party app governance; Least privilege; Token inventory.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-09 | Generic System Integrator / MSP SaaS data-theft and extortion profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: M-Trends 2026 highlights compromise of third-party SaaS vendors and use of stolen keys/PATs to pivot into downstream customers. Threat-led context: Salesloft Drift OAuth token compromise enabled access to Salesforce customer instances. Applicability=Third-Party SaaS; Phase=Initial Access / Pivot; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Generic phishing belongs to TP-07, ransomware/destructive encryption to TP-06, and supplier-side compromise to TP-10, though techniques are intentionally cross-referenced. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence of activity in a specific organisation.
